blocks.text: This guide provides information on configuring webhooks using Splunk Enterprise for Digital Experience (ZDX) alerts. The instructions provide a sample configuration that you can configure based on user requirements.

blocks.heading: Setting Up Webhooks in the Splunk Enterprise Instance

blocks.text: After your Splunk Enterprise instance has been installed and is running, follow this sequence to create webhooks:

blocks.item: Log in to your instance. The home page is displayed.
In the top-right corner of the page, click Settings.
See image.
Go to Data > Data inputs.
See image.

blocks.text: Configure HTTP Event Collector (HEC) to receive data:

blocks.item: Select HTTP Event Collector from the list of inputs.
See image.
In the top-right corner of the page, click Global Settings.
See image.
Configure the following Global Settings:
All Tokens: Select Enabled.
Default Source Type: Select _json.
Default Index: Select Default.
Default Output Group: Select None.
Deselect the Use Deployment Server checkbox.
Deselect the Enable SSL checkbox.
HTTP Port Number: Enter your HTTP Port Number.
Click Save.
See image.

blocks.text: To learn more about configuring HTTP Event Collector, refer to the Splunk Documentation.
Create a token to receive data:

blocks.item: In the top-right corner of the page, click New Token.
Enter a name for the token. Leave the remaining settings as shown in the following dialog:
See image.
Click Next.
Configure any additional input settings, then click Review.
Your settings are displayed for review.
See image.
Click Submit. A confirmation dialog displays the created token.
See image.
Highlight and copy the Token Value.

blocks.text: To configure a webhook in the Zscaler Admin Console:

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Digital Experience > Settings & Configurations > Webhooks.
Click Add Webhook.
In the Add Webhook window:
Name: Enter a webhook name for Splunk.
Status: Select Enabled to enable the webhook.
URL: Include the following parameter in your URL:
Authentication Type: Select Basic or Token.
For Basic, enter any string as the username, and enter the configured HEC Token Value from the previous step.
For Token, enter the configured HEC Token Value from the previous step as the Bearer Token.
Click Save and activate the changes.
